title: Request capture architecture & retention options - Lighthouse Health
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood request capture options (store vs storeless), redaction toggles, PII detection, KMS encryption and VPC/private deployment considerations. Customer is evaluating tradeoffs between ephemeral storeless and request-storage for a regulated telehealth workflow.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-11 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jasmin Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Reyes (Lighthouse - Security), Ben Caldwell (Platform Eng), Dr. Aaron Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): quick demo of the Console request-storage toggles, API flags for storeless mode, and discussion of redaction/PII heuristics. Action items: send security whitepaper, run a short storeless pilot with synthetic PHI, follow-up architecture diagram.

00:00:03 Jasmin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm jasmin with redwood, and ethan is our systems eng..
00:00:10 Maya: hi, thanks. we've got about an hour, want to focus on how you handle request capture and redaction for PHI, paritcularly retention controls.
00:00:20 Ethan: great — we'll start with the Console demo then show the API flags and talk through the architecture options for dedicated/private. bear with me while i share my screen.
00:00:45 [screen-share noise]
00:00:55 Ethan: ok — first slide is the request capture options. you can think of them as three modes: full request storage, storeless/ephemeral, and hybrid with selective ejection. full store retains request bodies for debugging and evals. storeless means we never persist PII to disk — we only keep ephemeral KV context in memory during the request lifecycle. hybrid lets you keep non-PII payloads and eject sensitive fields at ingest via redaction rules.
00:01:25 Ben: quick clarifying question — ephemeral: does that still allow for KV cache across tokens for session state? we run long medical dialogs.
00:01:35 Ethan: yeah good question. ephemeral storeless keeps KV cache in memory for the active session on the serving node — it doesn't get written to long term storage. so if the session is active, context is preserved. once the session cold stops or if the instance recycles, the in-memory cache is gone. that's why for long-running follow ups some customers use a hybrid where only hashed identifiers or non-PII fields are persisted.
00:02:05 Maya: what's the risk profile for storeless in terms of debugging and audits? regulators will ask for audit trails.
00:02:12 Jasmin: two quick notes: 1) For auditability we provide structured telemetry (request metadata, model/version, latency, token counts) to long-term logs even in storeless mode; actual request text can be redacted or withheld. 2) For regulated audits we offer an optional private control plane where audit logs and retention policies live inside your V P C — so you can provide auditors the telemetry without exposing raw PII.
00:02:48 Dr. Kim: do you have SOC2/ISO docs and a security whitepaper? that's the first ask from procurement.
00:02:55 Jasmin: yes — i'll drop the SOC2 and whitepaper link after. also we have a security playbook and a PHI handling guide. i'll add those to the follow-up.
00:03:10 Ethan: ok back to redaction. in the Console we have rule-based redaction and ML-assisted PII detection. rule-based is great for structured fields — e.g., ssn patterns, phone, emails. ml-assisted helps catch free-text PHI and names. both can be used together and run at ingest with configurable actions: redact, mask, hash, or drop.
00:03:40 Maya: is ML-assisted run locally or in your control plane? we need to ensure no PII leaves our network for detection.
00:03:48 Ethan: good restriction. for Private deployments (V P C / on-prem) the PII detection runs in your environment. for hosted customers we run detection in our region; if you need, we can offer a bring-your-own-detector hook where you run detection before the request hits our API.
00:04:10 Ben: if we use redaction rules, can we tune per route? some endpoints are higher risk (intake forms) and others are low risk (public FAQs).
00:04:18 Ethan: yes per-route policies are supported. you can create route profiles and attach a retention + redaction policy. in the Console it's a toggle matrix — rule sets per route, plus evaluation logs for redaction hits.
00:04:40 [15s pause as demo loads]
00:04:56 Ethan: i'll show the API flags briefly — there's request_storage: ["full","storeless","hybrid"], and a retain_fields list where you can specify allowlist of JSON paths. also a redact_on_ingest boolean and a pii_mode: ["rule","ml","hybrid"].
00:05:18 Maya: ok how are those stored? is the retain_fields enforced server-side or client-side?
00:05:25 Ethan: server-side enforcement. retain_fields is evaluated at ingestion and only those fields are written if in full/hybrid mode. for storeless mode retain_fields is ignored because we don't persist body. but you can still set the telemetry to capture hashes of retained keys for traceability.
00:05:45 Dr. Kim: hashes — are those reversible? we need determinism for de-dup but no reversibility for PHI.
00:05:52 Ethan: we use keyed HMACs via your KMS when in Private mode; the key lives in your KMS (BYOK pattern). so hashes are deterministic but you can't reverse them without the key and we can rotate keys per policy.
00:06:15 Maya: can you show the KMS integration?
00:06:20 Ethan: on the Console integrations page — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via standard connectors. in Private deployments the control plane never stores the plaintext key. you configure a key ARN and we use it to encrypt the persisted blobs and to HMAC fields.
00:06:40 Ben: what about audit logs — do they include redacted content, or just metadata?
00:06:46 Ethan: audit logs include metadata and an indicator if redaction ran and what rule triggered. we can also have a redaction-preview mode which shows the redacted output in the Console for engineering review (only visible to roles with permission). raw content can be stored in a dedicated secure bucket in your V P C for a limited retention window if required by policy.
00:07:16 Maya: retention windows — can you do per-field retention? e.g., keep non-PII for 365 days but drop PHI after 90 days.
00:07:24 Jasmin: yes — retention is policy driven and you can define policies at route, field, and model level. you can specify time-based rules and also event-based ejection.
00:07:35 [crosstalk]
00:07:45 Ethan: now the tradeoffs. full store gives you best debugging/eval capabilities and much simpler A/B testing and offline evals. cost is higher and risk increases for PII. storeless minimizes risk and cost for storage but makes debugging of subtle failures harder because you don't have raw text. hybrid is often preferred: persist sanitized transcripts and keep sensitive fields hashed or ejected.
00:08:12 Ben: from a cost perspective any ballpark?
00:08:16 Jasmin: generally storage is small compared to token compute for high-volume deployments, but if you retain full requests for long periods it adds up. our Optimize tooling can recommend compression, batch storage, and TTLs to reduce cost while keeping necessary data for evals. we'll run a quick analysis after you share sample traffic characteristics.
00:08:40 Maya: are there safeguards against accidental logging via debug flags? we don't want developers turning on verbose logs and leaking records.
00:08:49 Ethan: yes — RBAC and token-level enforcement. debug flags require a separate privileged token, and audit trails register who enabled them and when. we also support policy guards that prevent raw request persistence unless a compliance approval workflow is completed.
00:09:10 Dr. Kim: can you walk through a live redaction demonstration?
00:09:16 Ethan: sure — i'm switching to the Console. here is a sample request with PHI: "patient name: John Doe, dob, med notes..." i'm going to enable pii_mode: hybrid and redact_on_ingest true.
00:09:40 [keyboard sounds]
00:09:48 Ethan: ok sending...
00:09:52 Console (auto): redaction applied — name replaced with [REDACTED_NAME], ssn masked, phone hashed. redaction rule hit: rule-ssn-01.
00:10:05 Maya: that looks good — does the redaction pattern ever misfire on legitimate clinical terms? we've seen false positives on acronyms.
00:10:12 Ethan: there can be false positives. that's why we provide a redaction-preview and an allowlist to tune per route. ML-assisted mode has a confidence score so you can choose to only redact above a threshold. we log falsepositive counts in the Console so you can iterate.
00:10:36 Ben: for long running sessions — if we use hybrid and only persist hashed identifiers, can we rehydrate user state across sessions?
00:10:44 Ethan: yes — deterministic HMACs let you join sessions on identifiers without storing raw PII. you can instruct the runtime to store user state blobs referenced by HMAC keys, which are opaque ids.
00:11:05 Maya: how about egress controls — do you block model telemetry to external analytics services?
00:11:12 Jasmin: by default we emit aggregate telemetry to your metrics backend, but any export to third-party systems is gated. for Private deployments you control where telemetry goes; for hosted we can whitelist destinations.
00:11:30 Ethan: quick note on model rollouts: if you switch model variants, you can apply differential retention policies per model. e.g., smaller models for cheap inference and only log summaries, larger models for high-fidelity answers and optionally retain more context.
00:11:50 Dr. Kim: regarding the API — is there an SDK that wraps the redaction and field selectors so we don't leak from client-side?
00:11:58 Ethan: yes we have SDKs in node/python/java with a client-side sanitizer you can opt into. but remember client-side sanitation is defense-in-depth; server-side enforcement is the ultimate authority.
00:12:15 Maya: vendor risk — any third parties involved in the detection pipeline?
00:12:19 Jasmin: no third-party vendors process your raw PHI in Private. In hosted we may use internal ML services, but we can provide a dataflow diagram and contract clauses.
00:12:32 [15s pause]
00:12:48 Ethan: all right now quick architecture options: Hosted API (fastest deploy), Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput, isolated nodes but still managed control plane), Private (control plane in your V P C or fully on-prem). For strict regulatory requirements we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS BYOK.
00:13:15 Ben: does Private mean we run a control plane in our account and you ship runtime containers?
00:13:20 Jasmin: two models: 1) control plane in your V P C with our service components running as managed containers in your account; 2) fully on-prem bundle where you run both control plane and runtime. Both integrate with your KMS and audit tooling.
00:13:38 Maya: do you support air-gapped installs?
00:13:41 Ethan: yes — on-prem air-gapped is supported but requires an ops engagement. we provide scripts to preload models and compile artifacts; updates are handled via signed artifacts you pull through your internal registry.
00:13:56 Dr. Kim: ok from compliance side this is promising. one more thing: data residency — we operate in EU and need EU residency for storage.
00:14:05 Jasmin: we support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated; Private obviously keeps it in your region. we'll document exact region mappings in the follow-up.
00:14:20 Maya: curious about attack surface — if an attacker gains access to a node, can they dump in-memory KV cache and get sessions?
00:14:30 Ethan: it's a threat model we take seriously. on managed nodes we encrypt memory-backed swap and require strong mTLS between components. Dedicated and Private let you apply extra host-level controls. we also rotate ephemeral keys frequently and maintain a ffail-safe ejection policy: if a node is compromised we can evict sessions and force rekey.
00:14:58 Ben: what's the process to request a short pilot? we want to test storeless mode with simulated PHI and our UX flows.
00:15:06 Jasmin: typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 1 - integration and baseline metrics, week 2-3 - run synthetic traffic and adjust redaction rules, week 4 - evaluation and handoff. we'll provide a pilot SOW and a small engineering support allocation.
00:15:20 Dr. Kim: timelines — procurement wants cost estimates and SSO + SAML integration info.
00:15:26 Jasmin: i'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up along with our SAML docs and a sample SSO manifest.
00:15:35 [demo wrap-up]
00:15:40 Ethan: quick note on Optimize: it can scan traffic and recommend retention TTLs, compression, and whether hybrid or storeless gives best unit economics for you. it will also flag routes with high redaction false-positive rates for manual review.
00:15:58 Maya: love that. anything else?
00:16:05 Jasmin: we'll recap next steps — and then open for Q's.
00:16:12 [Q&A for remainder of call, snippets below]
00:16:20 Maya: if we go Private, who manages upgrades?
00:16:25 Ethan: upgrades are collaborative: we publish signed releases, you choose maintenance windows, and the Redwood field infra team can assist or manage upgrades under a support contract.
00:16:38 Ben: can we see a sample DB schema for persisted request blobs?
00:16:44 Ethan: yes — it's mainly metadata, encrypted payload, HMAC id, route id, model version and retention ttl. i'll attach an architecture diagram.
00:16:59 Dr. Kim: how do you validate redaction in automated tests?
00:17:05 Ethan: we provide a redaction test harness where you run sample corpora and get a report of hits, misses, and confidence distributions. it's part of the evals package.
00:17:20 Maya: any regulatory references for health? HIPAA?
00:17:25 Jasmin: we map features to HIPAA controls in the security playbook. it's not legal advice but it helps procurement evaluate technical controls.
00:17:36 [brief silence]
00:17:45 Maya: ok — last ask: can we get a minimal demo that shows storeless mode running with a simulated long session so we can observe ephemeral KV behavior and recovery patterns?
00:17:55 Jasmin: yes — we'll run a short bench with synthetic traffic and show the session termination behavior and logs.
00:18:05 Ethan: note: for long sessions we recommend pinning to dedicated nodes or sticky sessions; otherwise ephemeral state can be lost during autoscale.
00:18:18 Ben: we'll share a small sample of anonymized traffic and a requirements doc.
00:18:23 Jasmin: perfect. we'll follow up with SOW and docs.
00:18:30 [wrap and recap]
00:18:35 Jasmin: Recap and next steps: 1) Jasmin to send SOC2, security whitepaper, SAML SSO guide, and retention whitepaper. 2) Ethan to prepare pilot SOW and a short storeless bench plan. 3) Customer to share anonymized traffic sample and ROI targets. target dates below.
00:18:58 Maya: thanks all, talk soon.
00:19:02 [meeting ends — actual call length ~52 minutes — remaining time included Q&A and followups that were cut for brevity]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (V P C rendered as V P C, KV cache as K V cache), speaker labels mostly correct.
